name: KY-033 line tracking sensor
senses: a dark line or a bright surface under it
identification: Very narrow long black PCB with a small black infrared sensor block at one end, one white-and-blue round trim potentiometer, an 8-pin chip and 3 angled header pins.

confirmations.question: Read the 3 pin labels on the line tracking sensor. Are they G, +V and S?
confirmations.reason: Clone modules differ. The wiring plan is only valid for a module with these labels.

facts.statement: The module has three pins: ground (G), supply (+V) and signal (S). Go by the printed labels.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-033, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi, Pico or micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.

The signal is HIGH while the sensor is over a line (a light-absorbing surface) and LOW over a reflecting surface, where the LED on the module lights. Powered from 3.3 V the signal cannot rise above 3.3 V. The vendor's Arduino example switches on the board's internal pull-up resistor for this pin; LearnLens sketches do not, so whether the signal is stable without it is not confirmed.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-033, description and code example
